drhp.business: The Company operates in the auto components industry and is engaged in the production and manufacturing of seat frames and trims for four-wheeler and two-wheeler vehicles and other accessories relating to car seats. It is currently operating primarily under a single business segment manufacturing seat frames and seat trims for passenger cars as well as utility vehicles. Its operations are directly dependent on the growth of the Indian automotive industry, and it sells its products to group associate Bharat Seats Limited.
drhp.end_markets: Indian passenger cars and utility vehicles|Four-wheeler vehicles|Two-wheeler vehicles
drhp.expansion: FY2025-26 expansion was executed entirely through newly formed entities rather than disclosed capacity additions at existing sites. The Board, at its meeting on February 11, 2025, approved setting up a manufacturing facility for the project of seat insert fabric for four-wheelers, and for this project the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, NDR Auto Components Safety Systems Private Limited, with a Certificate of Incorporation dated May 13, 2025. risks.note: "The operations of the Company are directly dependent on the growth of the Indian automotive industry", so any moderation in vehicle demand flows straight through to the Company.
risks.risk: Business risk - dependence on the Indian automotive industry cycle

risks.note: "Any disruption of supply chain, availability of raw material could potentially impact the financial position and earnings of the Company."
risks.risk: Financial risk - supply chain disruption and raw material availability

risks.note: The Company is currently operating primarily under a single business segment manufacturing seat frames and seat trims for passenger cars and utility vehicles, leaving no diversification cushion within the existing business.
Sale of products in the related-party disclosure is essentially all to associate Bharat Seats Limited, so the revenue base is tied to a single group counterparty.

India's automotive industry in FY2025 reflected a normalisation pattern - two-wheelers recovered only gradually with rural demand sensitive to income cycles and financing, and commercial vehicles moderated in line with freight cycle normalisation.
risks.risk: Segment-mix and demand normalisation across vehicle categories

risks.note: BEV adoption alongside a resurgence of HEVs and PHEVs, plus expanded safety and fuel-economy regulation, continues to reshape platform requirements for component makers.
risks.risk: Powertrain transition - electrification reshaping platform requirements

risks.note: India's share of the $20 billion global automotive component trade remains modest at around 3%; operational costs, infrastructural gaps, moderate integration into global value chains and limited R&D expenditure continue to constrain competitiveness.
risks.risk: Structural competitiveness constraints of the Indian auto component sector

risks.note: "The Automobile industry will closely monitor macroeconomic factors and global geopolitics, which will determine the key demand conditions and supply chain dynamics going forward"; trade tensions, tighter financial conditions and geopolitical stress were flagged for 2025.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty affecting demand and supply chains

sk.overview: The industry covers control-intensive, critical-to-the-application electronic control units (ECUs) for the mobility (2/3-wheeler) and industrial (generator/genset) markets. In mobility, ECUs (ISG, EFI, ISG+EFI, EV motor control units) are indispensable to vehicle function; adoption is driven by regulation (emissions/efficiency) and OEM technology transitions, with Tier-I suppliers driving innovation.
